Answer routine HR questions without turning guidance into a decision

Give employees a privacy-conscious self-service front door for fictional balances and published policy examples, while keeping eligibility, sensitive circumstances, submissions, and HR decisions with authorized people and systems.

**Why try it:** The demo lets a employee ask a natural question and receive a source-backed, reviewable answer with the approval boundary visible in the response.

## Problem Statement

Employees wait for routine policy answers and HR teams repeat low-complexity guidance, yet personalization can expose sensitive data or overstep into eligibility decisions.

## Solution Summary

Copilot Studio and Microsoft Teams provide the employee experience; approved HRIS, benefits, and policy sources can be bound with identity, row-level security, data minimization, and audit controls.

**Blueprint role:** Establishes a safe self-service layer that separates policy explanation and draft preparation from protected HR transactions and decisions.

- **Leave-balance explanation** — Use when an employee asks for the fictional balance snapshot and published time-off rules.
- **Time-off draft preview** — Use when an employee wants to preview dates and projected balance before using the approved submission workflow.
- **Parental-leave policy guidance** — Use for published leave-policy questions without inferring a family or medical circumstance or deciding eligibility.
- **Health-plan policy explanation** — Use when an employee asks what the fictional plan snapshot says and what must be verified with benefits staff.
- **Remote-work policy guidance** — Use when an employee or manager asks for published remote-work rules without inferring a sensitive circumstance.
- **Benefits snapshot explanation** — Use when HR operations needs a concise fictional profile summary without estimating compensation or deciding eligibility.

The blueprint describes integration targets, not live connections in the packaged synthetic demo; see the [evidence boundary](../../solutions/ask-hr/FIELD-GUIDE.md#evidence-boundary).

## Business Outcomes

- Improves access to consistent policy guidance.
- Reduces repetitive explanation work for HR operations.
- Preserves privacy and human authority for individualized decisions.

Claims are qualitative; synthetic demo figures are not customer results or performance commitments. See the [claims policy](../../solutions/README.md#claims-policy).

## Target Users

| Role | Need |
| --- | --- |
| Employees | Understand the fictional leave balance and notice rules without treating the snapshot as a live entitlement. |
| Employees | Preview vacation dates and projected balance before using the approved submission workflow; the pilot submits nothing. |
| Employees | Understand the published parental-leave example without disclosing family details or receiving an eligibility decision. |
| Employees | Understand the fictional health-plan snapshot and which plan rules the benefits administrator must verify. |
| Managers | Explain the sample remote-work rules without inferring why an employee asked or making an individualized determination. |
| HR Operations Staff | Explain the fictional benefits profile consistently without estimating compensation or deciding eligibility. |

## In Scope / Out of Scope

### In scope

- Explain fictional leave balances, holidays, accrual, rollover and notice rules from the fixed Ask HR snapshot.
- Preview vacation dates and projected balances as `Not Submitted`, `Draft for employee review`, and `No notification was sent`.
- Explain published parental-leave examples and identify HR verification needs without determining eligibility or asking for family details.
- Summarize fictional health-plan and enrollment rules, naming checks for benefits staff rather than recommending a plan.
- Explain published remote-work rules without inferring an employee's reasons or sensitive circumstances.
- Summarize the fictional benefits profile without estimating salary, total compensation or eligibility.

### Out of scope / approval boundary

- No real employee records, live HRIS or benefits lookups, or access to Outlook, Teams or a manager workflow; only the uploaded synthetic snapshot is used.
- No browsing or external policy, legal, medical, payroll or current-date facts; the packaged policy examples are not live guidance.
- No eligibility or employment decisions, health-plan recommendations or approval of exceptions; individualized determinations belong to authorized HR staff.
- No inference of pregnancy, disability, caregiver or family status, and no matching a fictional profile to a real employee.
- No time-off submission, manager notification, HR record change or completed transaction; the time-off operation produces a reviewable draft only.
- No salary or total-compensation estimates from the fictional benefits profile.
- No workshop publishing: keep Ask HR in Draft until an authorized reviewer validates every operation and guardrail and separately approves publication.

## Qualification Checklist

- [ ] Is a Microsoft Copilot Studio target environment, with an approved publisher prefix, available for the Ask HR build?
- [ ] Can the delivery team authenticate with PAC CLI 2.9.3 or newer, initialize `cli-copilot`, and preserve the generated agent identity?
- [ ] Has the customer decided whether Outlook and Microsoft Teams belong in the production HR workflow, separately from the synthetic workshop?
- [ ] Have security, privacy and the HR business owner approved the HRIS, benefits and policy sources that will replace the synthetic files?
- [ ] Are dedicated connection references and least-privilege access approved for each selected HR system, with the reviewed input and output contract preserved?
- [ ] Are authorized HR and benefits reviewers identified for individualized eligibility, exceptions and any proposed transaction?
- [ ] Is publication held for separate approval after replaying every locked HR case against the reviewed instructions, knowledge, skills and model?
- [ ] Have governance, telemetry, support and success measures been agreed for the production HR service?

## What Actually Goes Wrong

| Issue | Response |
| --- | --- |
| Manual skill-upload and inventory screenshots do not show every required HR skill. | Restore Easy/Manual inventory parity, then recapture the missing skill chips and saved inventory with all six HR skills, both knowledge files, the reviewed model and no tools. |
| HR instructions are visible, but the save checkpoint has no saved-state indicator. | Reshoot the save step with a visible saved-state indicator; visible policy text alone does not prove the save completed. |
| The assisted Draft screenshot shows unrelated agents, not the Ask HR agent under review. | Withhold the frame and capture the named Ask HR agent row with its Draft badge; keep publication behind separate authorization. |
| HR-02 screenshots omit exact draft-status phrases, so a plausible time-off preview is mistaken for a full pass. | Check the final response against every locked marker, including `Not Submitted`, `Draft for employee review` and `No notification was sent`; replay the same corpus in Copilot Studio. |
| An HR skill or its knowledge cannot be loaded, but the agent tries to answer from remembered policy values. | Use the exact routing-map skill name. After one retry in the same turn, report the loading failure and stop; do not replace missing citations with general knowledge. |
| Ask HR Preview runs while the synthetic policy and profile files are still processing. | Wait for ingestion to finish before Preview; do not accept a partial answer as evidence. |
| An employee asks the pilot to decide eligibility, infer family circumstances or notify a manager. | Keep the answer within the synthetic policy snapshot, decline the decision or action, and route individualized determinations to authorized HR staff through the approved workflow. |
| An HR case lacks required evidence or its recorded identifier, despite a working import or plausible demo answer. | Stop and mark the case failed. Restore or capture real evidence, investigate missing identifiers, then replay unchanged cases after correction; never use mockups or retry until a case happens to pass. |
